title: Pancreas
source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion; 17.9 The Endocrine Pancreas

main.t: A gland behind the stomach that makes digestive juice for the duodenum and hormones that control blood glucose.

simpler.t: Your pancreas makes juices to digest food and insulin to manage sugar in your blood.

deeper.t: It is both exocrine (enzymes into ducts) and endocrine (hormones into the blood).

facts.t: It lies across the back of the abdomen, behind the stomach, in the retroperitoneum.
Its head sits in the C-shaped curve of the duodenum; its tail reaches the spleen.

simpler.t: It lies flat behind your stomach, from the duodenum across to the spleen.

deeper.t: Its body extends about 15 cm to the left of the head.

items.name: Head, body and tail
items.t: Head in the duodenal curve, body extending left, tail at the hilum of the spleen.

items.name: Acini
items.t: Grape-like clusters of cells that make pancreatic juice.

items.name: Pancreatic islets
items.t: Islands of endocrine cells among the acini (formerly the islets of Langerhans).

items.name: Pancreatic ducts
items.t: The main duct joins the bile duct at the hepatopancreatic ampulla. A smaller accessory duct may open separately.

simpler.t: Mostly juice-making cells, with small islands of hormone-making cells.

deeper.t: In each islet, beta cells (insulin) make up about 75 percent and alpha cells (glucagon) about 20 percent.

facts.t: It makes over a litre of pancreatic juice a day; its bicarbonate buffers the acidic chyme.
Protein-digesting enzymes are made inactive, so they cannot digest the pancreas itself.
Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.

simpler.t: Its juice neutralises stomach acid and digests food; its hormones balance blood sugar.

items.name: Duodenum
items.t: Curves round the head of the pancreas and receives its juice.

items.name: Common bile duct
items.t: Joins the main pancreatic duct just before the duodenum.

items.name: Stomach
items.t: Lies in front of the pancreas.

items.name: Spleen
items.t: The tail of the pancreas ends at its hilum.

items.name: Cholecystokinin
items.t: From I cells of the duodenum; stimulates the release of pancreatic juices and bile.

simpler.t: It is wrapped by the duodenum and shares a duct with the liver.

facts.t: It develops from buds of the embryonic gut tube that later fuse.
facts.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). The development of the pancreas.

facts.t: A smaller accessory duct, when present, opens into the duodenum about 2.5 cm (1 inch) above the main opening.

items.injury: Protein-digesting enzymes activated inside the pancreas.
items.cannotDo: Digest food normally, while the inflamed gland is painful.
items.why: Active enzymes digest the pancreatic tissue.
items.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). The symptoms of pancreatitis.

items.injury: An autoimmune attack on the beta cells.
items.damaged: The beta cells of the islets (type 1 diabetes).
items.cannotDo: Make insulin: they need insulin by injection or infusion.
items.why: Without insulin, glucose cannot enter most body cells.

items.q: Explain why the pancreas makes its protein-digesting enzymes in inactive forms.
model: Active enzymes would digest the pancreas.
They are released as trypsinogen and other inactive forms.
Enteropeptidase in the duodenum activates trypsin.
Trypsin then activates the other enzymes.
Insulin comes from beta cells; glucagon from alpha cells.
High blood glucose releases insulin; low glucose releases glucagon.
Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.
Both are controlled by negative feedback.

items.q: Predict what happens to the beta cells in long-standing type 2 diabetes.
model: Body cells become resistant to insulin.
The pancreas makes more insulin to compensate.
Over time the beta cells become exhausted.

check.why: Beta cells, about 75 percent of each islet, produce insulin.

check.stem: What makes pancreatic juice slightly alkaline?
check.why: Sodium bicarbonate gives pancreatic juice its alkalinity.

check.stem: Where does the head of the pancreas lie?
options: At the hilum of the spleen
In the C-shaped curve of the duodenum
check.why: Its head nestles in the C-shaped curve of the duodenum.
